name: SurveyMonkey
tagline: Online survey platform for market research and feedback.
description: SurveyMonkey is a survey and feedback platform for building questionnaires, collecting responses, and reporting on the answers received.
pros: Templates and a question library shorten the path from a feedback need to a survey that can go out the same day
Skip logic routes respondents past questions that do not apply to them, which is what keeps completion usable on longer instruments
Panel recruitment is available for teams that need answers from people outside their own contact list
Results accumulate into tables while the survey is still open, so a program can be read mid-flight
The freemium model with a recorded band of $39-99/mo gives an entry point before any vendor conversation
cons: Analysis stops at breakdowns and cross-tabs: research needing weighting or advanced statistics has to move to another tool
Responses do not attach to a customer record on their own, so findings must be carried into a system of record to affect decisions
Certification, retention terms, and residency options are all missing from this repository's record for SurveyMonkey

features.name: Survey and question builder
features.description: Assembles instruments from question types with option sets and validation. The full type inventory is not listed in this dataset.

features.name: Skip logic and branching
features.description: Routes respondents around questions that do not apply, based on prior answers. per-plan ceilings are absent from the material used here.

features.name: Link, email, and embed distribution
features.description: Shares a survey by URL, by invitation, or by placement on a page. Invitation limits are not captured in these fields.

features.name: Panel response recruitment
features.description: Buys responses from respondents recruited to a profile when the existing list cannot answer. Panel pricing is not recorded in this repository.

features.name: Live results tables
features.description: Answers aggregate into charts and tables while the survey is open. Cross-tab depth is not itemized in this dataset.

features.name: Filtering by respondent attributes
features.description: Cuts results by respondent attributes or by answers to see subgroups. The available filter types are not listed here.

features.name: Raw response export
features.description: Moves response rows out for analysis in another system. File formats and row limits are not enumerated in these fields.

features.name: API for response data
features.description: Programmatic endpoints for pulling responses into other systems. Endpoint coverage and named connectors are not itemized in this repository.

content.title: SurveyMonkey as the survey layer
content.body: SurveyMonkey is a survey and feedback platform, and the whole product is the questionnaire, its distribution, and the answers that come back. That puts it in a different job from the marketing automation this repository files in the same category: Marketo moves people through nurture programs, while SurveyMonkey asks them a question and reports what they said. This dataset files SurveyMonkey under Marketing & SEO with a freemium pricing model, a band of $39-99/mo, and a descriptor of an online survey platform for market research and feedback.

content.title: Templates, question types, and skip logic
content.body: Construction starts from a template or a blank page: question types for rating, choice, ranking, and free text, with skip logic that routes a respondent past the questions that do not apply to them. The question library is the part of a survey tool that pays off over years, because carefully worded questions get reused across feedback cycles rather than rewritten each time. This repository does not itemize which question types or logic rules ship in which plan, so the depth of branching and validation belongs on a vendor checklist rather than in an assumption.

content.title: Panels, links, and how responses arrive
content.body: Responses arrive through one of several doors, and the door changes what the answers mean. A recruited panel answers a general question in exchange for the incentive, while an invited list answers about a relationship the organization already has, which is usually the more actionable of the two. This dataset records neither panel pricing nor recruitment controls, so the difference between collecting from your own audience and buying a sample has to be priced with the vendor rather than inferred from the plan fields.
items: A shared link posted anywhere the audience already reads
An email invitation sent to a list the organization already holds
An embedded survey placed on a page or inside a message
A panel of recruited respondents bought for the question at hand

content.title: Reading the results: reports and exports
content.body: Results land in tables and charts as answers accumulate, with filtering by respondent attributes and an export for anyone who wants the raw rows. Export quality is the quiet differentiator in this repository's records: the Typeform review held in this dataset notes export options limited compared with dedicated survey tools like SurveyMonkey, which puts this product on the stronger side of that particular comparison. Where responses go next — into a CRM, a spreadsheet, or a reporting tool — depends on connectors this repository does not enumerate, so confirm the current integration list with the vendor.

content.title: Free tier and the $39-99/mo record
content.body: SurveyMonkey is recorded here under a freemium pricing model with a band of $39-99/mo: a free entry point followed by paid tiers. What the band does not say is what the free tier caps — responses, questions, or collaborators — nor what a panel costs when a team buys a sample. The same band appears in this repository's survey-tools and form-builders listings, so the figure is at least consistent across the dataset. This page is assembled from SurveyMonkey's published documentation and the records this repository holds for the product, so treat the band as a stored reference and check current published pricing before budgeting.

content.title: Limits that come with a form-first tool
content.body: A form-first tool has boundaries worth naming. It is the wrong shape for longitudinal research that needs panel management, sophisticated weighting, or statistical treatment beyond basic breakdowns, and it does not own the customer record the way a CRM does, so findings have to be carried elsewhere before they change a decision. The security posture is a second boundary: this repository holds no certification entry, no retention schedule, no residency term, or identity detail for SurveyMonkey, and survey responses frequently include personal or employee data. Neither boundary is resolved by the pricing fields.

content.title: Typeform, Marketo, and where SurveyMonkey fits
content.body: In this dataset SurveyMonkey is compared against Marketo, Optimizely, ActiveCampaign, Ahrefs, ConvertKit, Mailchimp, Moz, and SEMrush, with Typeform as the closest recorded counterpart in the form-and-survey space. The fit question is simpler. SurveyMonkey suits teams whose immediate need is to ask a defined group a question and see the answers — recurring feedback, candidate and employee surveys, event follow-up — and does not suit research programs that need sampling rigor or buyers who need certification evidence this dataset does not carry.

faqs.question: How does SurveyMonkey differ from Marketo?
faqs.answer: Marketo runs nurture programs and lead scoring; SurveyMonkey collects answers to questions. Both sit in this repository's Marketing & SEO category, but a team buying one is not replacing the other.

faqs.question: Is there a free version of SurveyMonkey?
faqs.answer: This dataset records SurveyMonkey under a freemium model with a band of $39-99/mo. What the free tier limits — responses, questions, or collaborators — is not captured here; check the vendor's current packaging.

faqs.question: Can SurveyMonkey recruit respondents for us?
faqs.answer: Panel recruitment is available for teams that need answers from people outside their own list. Panel pricing and screening controls are not recorded in this repository, so price them with the vendor.

faqs.question: How does SurveyMonkey compare with Typeform?
faqs.answer: Typeform is recorded here as stronger on question presentation, while this repository's Typeform review notes that its export options are limited compared with dedicated survey tools like SurveyMonkey.

faqs.question: What does this repository record about SurveyMonkey security?
faqs.answer: Nothing in the way of certification, retention schedule, or residency term appears in the fields held for SurveyMonkey. Since responses often carry personal data, check it against documentation the vendor currently publishes.

author: Emily Nakamura
learningCurve: Building and sending a survey is quick; question design, logic, and analysis rigor are where experience shows.
whoShouldUse: Teams that need to ask a defined audience a question and get structured answers back — recurring feedback, employee and candidate surveys, event follow-up — including organizations that may buy panel responses.
whoShouldNotUse: Research programs that need sampling control, weighting, or statistical treatment beyond basic breakdowns, teams that need responses attached automatically to a customer record, and buyers requiring documentation of certification this repository does not hold.
